Me or the Machine

If an AI writes one sentence in my voice, can the people closest to me tell it is not me?
Jaideep Aher, Duke University, AIPI 590 Responsible AI, fall 2026
Take the test, see the charts

The problem

My speech is recorded

A wearable turns every conversation into text.

The transcripts leak

A breach, an export or a malicious app copies them.

An AI learns my voice

A language model writes new lines that sound like me.

A friend gets a text

"Lost my card, can you send me 200?" Do they notice?

How the test worked

I took 48 real lines from my own wearable, after removing anything private. A language model read them and wrote 47 twin lines. Ten people who know me saw one shuffled line at a time and chose "really him" or "AI twin", with no answers until the end. Everyone knew some lines were fake.

49%
of 160 saved judgments were right. A coin flip.
78 of 160, 95% interval 41% to 56%, p = 0.81. Per judge: mean 49%. With three reported 30-line scores: 111 of 250 (44%).
Right (78)Wrong (82)50% mark

Evidence of no skill, not too little data

Could this sample catch real skill?Yes. A true accuracy of 61% would show 80% of the time.
Accuracy within 50% ± 10?Yes. Equivalence test p = 0.015.
Guessing or some ability?Guessing, about 10 times more likely (Bayes factor).
Can a style detector do better?No. 59% on all 95 lines, p = 0.11.

Friends didn't agree

Said "him"Said "AI"Columns: the 20 shared lines

Agreement was below chance (Fleiss' κ = -0.17). Majority vote: right on 3, wrong on 5, tied on 12.

Twin lines passed as often

Sensitivity d′ = -0.06: zero means no ability to tell them apart. Friends said "him" 57.5% of the time, a lean towards trust that helps an impostor.

Nobody was reliably good

Each dot is one judge. Only one scored above 50% (14 of 20, not significant alone).

Above 50%BelowReported score, not saved

What it means

Short messages are the weak spot

The cheapest attack is one short text, the exact format where people who know me failed.

Trust works against us

Friends default to "it's him". An impostor only needs to not sound wrong.

Recorded speech is sensitive data

Treat wearable transcripts like a password: on the device, kept briefly.

Agree a check in advance

A question only the real person can answer beats trying to spot style.

Limits. Ten judges; three 30-line scores were reported, not saved. Twin lines were written with my real lines in view, the best case for the twin. Next: a control twin that knows nothing about me, and longer conversations.
Ethics. Every judge knew some lines were AI-written; no message was ever sent as me; judges are anonymised. Related work. Turing (1950), Computing Machinery and Intelligence. Jones and Bergen (2025), Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test. Park et al. (2024), Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People.
